decisions.statement: A process is named by a list with the command and its arguments.
Each stream a process says on is taken whole.
A code other than zero is answered as data.
A process ending on a signal is answered as `-1` and the name of that signal.
A process ending on a code of its own is answered as naming no signal.
How a process ended is spelled once here as a code or as a signal.
A throw says how the process ended rather than a code alone.
A caller wanting a throw asks for the streams rather than how the process ran.
A process inherits the environment of its caller.
An environment stated replaces the environment inherited.
A process's output stream is answered as bytes where bytes are asked for.
Text is those bytes read as text rather than a second run.
A process is answered with the processor seconds that process spent.
A process is answered with the peak memory that process reached.
That peak is the highest everything in the process's group ever held at once.
The group's peak is read once the process ended and before the group is taken away.
A caller is answered whether the peak answered was measured.
A process run in no group is answered as having reached no peak.
Such a process is answered as having had no peak measured.
A process is answered the seconds every process in that process's group spent.
Those seconds carry a child the run never reaped.
The seconds answered leave out what was spent before the run joined its group.
A bounded process is answered the seconds its ceiling is judged against.
A process run in no group is answered the seconds that process and its reaped children spent.
The group's seconds are read before the group is taken away.
A process the kernel reported no usage for is answered as having spent no seconds.
A caller may give a process a ceiling in processor seconds.
A process ended for running away is answered as having died on a signal.
A ceiling bounds a process together with everything that process starts.
A caller may give a process a ceiling in megabytes of memory.
A process at its memory ceiling is reclaimed and slowed rather than ended.
A memory ceiling is stated on the group before the run joins that group.
A run given no memory ceiling is held to none.
A caller may ask that a process be measured.
A process asked to be measured, or given a ceiling, runs in a control group made for that one run.
Every other process runs in the group its caller is already in.
Making a group and taking it away costs several times what a short run costs.
The run sits in a leaf of that group, and what the run starts sits beside it.
What a run spent and held is read from that group rather than from the leaf.
A run started inside a run makes its group under that run's group.
A memory ceiling on a group above a run bounds the peak that run is answered.
That group is made under the nearest ancestor group this run may write in.
The mount every group hangs under is never that ancestor.
An ancestor group is written in only where processor time and memory are delegated to that group.
A group left where the run that made it is gone is taken away before a group is made.
A group left is known by the run that made it being named in the group's name.
Groups left are looked for in the group this process makes its own groups in.
A group left is taken away with every group inside it.
Every process still in a group left is ended before that group is taken away.
A group whose name names a process now running outside the group's parent is a group left.
A group this process sits in is never taken away as left.
A group under a container's group is left alone.
No group another container made is ever taken away as left.
A group that cannot be taken away once its run is over is said aloud on the error stream.
A group left goes at the next group made beside it or at the reaper's next tick.
The program a process is named by is looked for on the path before the run.
A program is looked for on the path the run itself will have.
A program found is run by the path that found it.
A program found nowhere is run in no group.
The seconds a bounded process's group has spent are read while the run is going.
Every process in the group is ended at once where those seconds go past twice the ceiling.
A run is ended at twice the ceiling its caller stated rather than at that ceiling.
A run over its stated ceiling and under twice it runs to its own end.
The seconds such a run is answered are what its caller reads its stated ceiling against.
The group is taken away once the run is over whatever the run said.
A ceiling raises no limit.
Nothing ends a process whose caller stated no ceiling.
A machine delegating processor time and memory nowhere bounds no run.
A run on such a machine is not refused.
A run on such a machine is caught by the seconds answered rather than bounded.
A run on such a machine has no peak measured.
A run inside a run states a ceiling of its own.
A process given no ceiling runs to its own end.
Every run is made in the process asking for it.
No process started here is meant to outlive its starter.
The process running here may be held to a memory ceiling of its own.
A process held here sits in a leaf of the group made for that hold.
The memory ceiling of a hold is stated on that leaf.
A hold answers a way to let the process go.
Letting go moves the process back to the group it was held out of.
Letting go takes away the group the hold made.
A process is held only where the group it came from would take that process back.
A hold that could not be made answers a letting go that does nothing.
Nothing raises where a process cannot be held.
A Go program reads its own group for a processor quota and consults no group above it.
A group held to a memory ceiling and a quota at once cannot reclaim its way under that ceiling.
A run given a group of its own is given the processors its quota buys as `GOMAXPROCS`.
That count is stated in the run's environment rather than on the run's group.
The quota is the tightest any group above the run states rather than the nearest one stated.
A quota buying part of a processor is given as one processor rather than as none.
A run no group above holds to a quota is given the environment its caller stated.
A caller stating that count itself is left the count that caller stated.

definition: a process run to its end, and the code and streams it leaves
